Dangerous combinations

BRACE item B05 · Destructive-action interception asks you to record which agents can read outside text, reach private data or change things, and talk to the outside, all in one context. When one agent can do all of these, treat every action it takes as high-impact.

  1. PresentCan be tricked into leaking data

    billing-agent reads text that an outsider can write (accounting). It can also reach private data (invoices database) and send data out (mail API). Hidden instructions in that outside text could make it copy the private data and send it away.

    • outside text accounting (inferred)
    • private data invoices database (reviewer)
    • sends out mail API (reviewer)

    Also reaches: outside text: negotiation memory (Redis); private data: negotiation memory (Redis), policy search database; sends out: payments API, ticket API.

    Capabilities unknown for: draft_letter.

    Fix one way: (1) Remove a tool the agent does not need for this task. (2) Split the work into separate agents, so no single agent has all of these. (3) Add a human approval step before it sends or acts. (4) Limit what the sending or acting tool can reach (fixed destinations, fixed accounts, allowlists).

    See BRACE item B05 · Destructive-action interception.

  2. PresentCan be tricked into harmful actions

    billing-agent reads text that an outsider can write (accounting). It can also change or delete things, or move money (payments API). Hidden instructions in that outside text could make it take a harmful action.

    • outside text accounting (inferred)
    • changes or deletes payments API (reviewer)

    Also reaches: outside text: negotiation memory (Redis); changes or deletes: issue_refund.

    Capabilities unknown for: draft_letter.

    Fix one way: (1) Remove a tool the agent does not need for this task. (2) Split the work into separate agents, so no single agent has all of these. (3) Add a human approval step before it sends or acts. (4) Limit what the sending or acting tool can reach (fixed destinations, fixed accounts, allowlists).

    See BRACE item B05 · Destructive-action interception.

Most urgent first: by gate, then by how many connections and dangerous combinations the fix touches. Open “How to fix” for the steps.
ItemGateWhat is wrongWhereLead role
R02
Separate data from instructions and test injection containment		Blocker
Needs proof		Text from the accounting server and saved notes reaches the model, but there is no test showing an attack in that text is stopped.

Affects 4 connections, 2 dangerous combinations.

How to fix
  1. Write ten fake tool results that tell the agent to send a refund or an email.
  2. Feed each one to the agent in a test setup, not in production.
  3. Repeat each one five times and count how often the agent obeys.
  4. Save the results with the date and the code version.

Done when: A dated test record shows how often attacks in tool text work, and none of them moved money or sent email.

accounting, negotiation memory (Redis)Security
E08
Bounded delegated authority		Blocker
Gap		The letter-writing helper agent is meant to have no tools, but it gets all of them, including refunds and email.

Affects 6 connections, 1 dangerous combination.

How to fix
  1. Open src/tools/registry.py and find scoped (line 41).
  2. Change it so an empty list gives back a registry with no tools.
  3. Add a test: make a scoped registry with an empty list and check that it has zero tools.
  4. Run the drafter once and check the log shows no tool calls.

Done when: The drafter cannot call any tool, and the new test passes.

Where in the code: src/tools/registry.py:41

src/drafter.py, issue_refundAgent team
B05
Destructive-action interception		Blocker
Gap		The agent can email any address, give credits with no approval, and refund up to $500 with no approval.

Affects 4 connections, 1 dangerous combination.

How to fix
  1. Make a list of actions that move money or send messages outside: refunds, credits and emails.
  2. For each one, ask a person to approve it before it runs.
  3. Only send email to the customer's address on file. Refuse any other address.
  4. Send email as plain text, not HTML, so it cannot load images or links from other sites.
  5. Add a test for each action that runs it with no approval. Each one should be refused.

Done when: Refunds, credits and emails to new addresses all wait for a person to approve them.

Where in the code: src/tools/comms.py:17

send_reminder, mail API, issue_creditAgent team
B06
Approval integrity		Blocker
Gap		One approval for a small refund can be reused to refund any amount, many times.

Affects 4 connections, 1 dangerous combination.

How to fix
  1. Open src/tools/payments.py and find the line that looks up the approval (line 73).
  2. Save the approved amount with each approval when it is created.
  3. Before a refund runs, check that the refund amount is not more than the approved amount.
  4. Check that the approval was made for this same run.
  5. Mark the approval as used right after the refund. Refuse any approval that is already used.
  6. Add a test that tries a bigger refund with a small approval. The test should fail the refund.

Done when: A refund larger than its approval is refused, and an approval cannot be used twice.

Where in the code: src/tools/payments.py:73

issue_refund, payments APIAgent team
A04
Trustworthy attribution		Blocker
Gap		The model can choose which customer company gets a credit, so it could credit another company's account.

Affects 3 connections, 1 dangerous combination.

How to fix
  1. Open src/tools/payments.py and go to line 91.
  2. Delete the part that reads tenant_id from the tool arguments.
  3. Always use the tenant from the run, ctx.tenant_id.
  4. Remove tenant_id from the tool's input fields so the model cannot send it.
  5. Add a test that sends a different tenant_id. The credit must go to the run's own tenant or be refused.

Done when: No tool argument can change which tenant gets a credit.

Where in the code: src/tools/payments.py:91

issue_credit, payments APIAgent team
B03
Credential lifetime and handling		Required
Gap		A secret login token for the accounting server is saved in a settings file in the code.

Affects 2 connections, 2 dangerous combinations.

How to fix
  1. Ask the accounting team to cancel (revoke) the token in config/agent.yaml line 50 today.
  2. Delete the token from the file.
  3. Store a new token in the company secret store, not in the code.
  4. Change the agent so it stops if no token is found, instead of using a saved one.
  5. Use a token that expires within a day if the accounting server allows it.

Done when: No token is in the code, the old token no longer works, and the agent reads its token from the secret store.

Where in the code: config/agent.yaml:50

accountingInfrastructure
E06
Enforced gateway boundary		Required
Gap		The agent talks straight to the accounting server. Nothing in between checks, limits or logs each call.

Affects 2 connections, 2 dangerous combinations.

How to fix
  1. Choose a gateway that sits between the agent and the accounting server.
  2. Set it to check who is calling and which tool they may use.
  3. Set a limit on how many calls the agent can make each minute.
  4. Turn on a log entry for every call.
  5. Change the address in .mcp.json so the agent connects to the gateway, not the server.

Done when: Every accounting call goes through the gateway and shows up in its log.

Where in the code: .mcp.json:5

accountingInfrastructure
R05
Memory isolation and write validation		Detection
Gap		Saved notes are filed by email address only, so two customer companies with the same contact share notes.

Affects 4 connections.

How to fix
  1. Open src/memory.py and go to line 25.
  2. Add the tenant to the key, so it looks like neg:<tenant>:<email>.
  3. Move or delete old notes that use the old key.
  4. Mark notes the agent wrote itself as not trusted, so they are not treated as facts later.
  5. Add a test with two tenants and the same email. Each must see only its own notes.

Done when: One tenant can never read or change another tenant's notes.

Where in the code: src/memory.py:25

What this page does not show

  • It is built from reading code and settings. It does not prove the agent is safe when it runs.
  • “Undeclared” means the settings do not list it. Code the reviewer did not trace is not on the map.
  • Script-derived first pass from .mcp.json, the candidate inventory and agent config. Trust zones, boundary crossings, data flows and components reached only through code (databases, HTTP APIs, queues) are not established. No code was executed.
